newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Press Digest - Ireland - January 16.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - Ireland - January 16.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- It will take up to four years before scientists can say with any certainty how large the epidemic of CJD, the human form of BSE, will be.
- Irish farmers took to the streets to protest Wednesday's 10 percent cut by the EU Commission in export refunds, which has thrown the beef markets into chaos.

- German authorities seeking the extradition from Ireland of the Belfast actor, James Corry, in connection with the IRA mortar attack on Osnabrueck last June maintained he was "a British citizen" in their documents.
- The value of Irish beef exports fell by around 150 million Irish pounds during 1996 as a result of the BSE crisis.

- A heavily armed German who shot three men as they tried to evict him and his terminally ill mother from a County Cavan cottage was on Wednesday night surrounded by armed detectives in a tense siege.
- The biggest tax giveaway budget in the history of Ireland will be unveiled next week.
- Car cover could increase by up to 10 percent this year because of a backlog of accident claims, Ireland's second largest insurer Hibernian warned on Wednesday.
- The Irish Prime Minister John Bruton on Wednesday pressed the EU Commission to reverse its decision to cut beef export aid by 10 percent.
